solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leader fitting in second man

indicators.note: fitting in tells us the word for fitting goes inside the second man

parts.note: in Genesis Cain is the first son of Adam, so the second man
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A team leader slots in a deputy as his number two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second man' reads like a deputy, but it is Cain, the second man after Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the person in charge of a team, ship or company, its leader.

clue.text: Regulator tracks second item for the party?

parts.note: a cock (as in stopcock) is a valve that regulates flow
to tail someone is to track them, so tails means tracks
a tick is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A device that regulates tracks every second, oddly said to be for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A cock is a tap or valve regulating flow, as in stopcock.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spike used to spear olives or nibbles, a typical piece of kit at a drinks gathering.

clue.text: Here, item under the tree?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in attendance, not absent
second meaning: a gift left beneath the Christmas tree

explanation.walkthrough: One word as an adjective means in attendance; as a noun it is a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Present means in attendance at roll-call, and it is also a gift, as left beneath a Christmas tree.

clue.text: Enough drink has overwhelmed parliamentarian

indicators.note: the drink has overwhelmed, swallowing up, the parliamentarian, so it goes around him

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
MP is the abbreviation for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has had one too many and is overcome by drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plenty, more than sufficient, so it stands for enough.

clue.text: That's OK under no circumstances

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a polite reply to thanks, it was no trouble
second meaning: in no way whatsoever

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both a polite reply to thanks and an emphatic negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Said after 'thank you' the phrase waves away gratitude; elsewhere it is an emphatic never or in no way.

clue.text: Calculator, perhaps, passing fifty — might that be to scale?

indicators.note: the calculator is passing fifty, so the fifty comes first and it follows on

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an adder is something that adds, a calculator for example

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a calculator's reading past fifty is drawn to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To scale' sounds like proportional drawing, but scale here means climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is equipment used for climbing up, that is for scaling a wall or height.

clue.text: Stuffed — like a fat cat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: filled up, packed full
second meaning: very rich, as a fat cat (wealthy executive) is

explanation.walkthrough: A fat cat is slang for a wealthy, overpaid boss; loaded is slang for rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded means filled full of something, and in slang it also means extremely wealthy, like a highly paid executive.

clue.text: Strip cartoon ultimately embraced by lads, item that's vulgar

indicators.note: the cartoon's last letter is held within the letters of lads and item
vulgar in the sense of coarse or broken up signals that these letters are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of cartoon

explanation.surface: A rude strip cartoon gets passed round a group of lads as a crude item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip cartoon' looks like a comic strip, but Strip alone is the definition; 'vulgar' is the anagram signal, in its old sense of common or corrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a machine is to take it apart piece by piece, which is to dismantle it.

clue.text: Stone me! River saved in remarkable deal

indicators.note: kept safe within, so me and river go inside the other letters
remarkable here suggests the letters of deal are remarked, set out anew

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a river being protected by an extraordinary agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' reads as a British exclamation of surprise, but Stone alone is the definition and 'me' is fodder; 'remarkable' works as re-markable, set out afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious gem, so it is a type of stone in the jeweller's sense.

clue.text: Queen moved to palace where king shackled

indicators.note: the king is shackled, held fast inside the other letters
moved signals that the letters of to palace are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A queen relocated to a palace where a king was held in chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling monarch of Ptolemaic Egypt, a famous historical female sovereign.

clue.text: Effort you and I put into day

indicators.note: put into tells us you and I are placed inside the day

parts.note: SAT is the abbreviation for Saturday
we means you and I together

explanation.surface: Two people commit their effort to a single day's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat stands for hard work or exertion, as in blood, sweat and tears.

clue.text: Thoughtful card, offered hugs

indicators.note: the word for offered hugs, wraps itself around, the card

parts.note: to tender is to offer, so offered is tendered
a heart is a playing card of that suit

explanation.surface: A kind greeting card arrives with hugs attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' suggests a greeting card, but it is a heart from a pack of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tender-hearted is kind and considerate of others' feelings, that is thoughtful.

clue.text: Subject, maths originally introduced to you

indicators.note: introduced to means put into the word for you

parts.note: thee is the old form of you

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letter of maths

explanation.surface: A teacher brings in a mathematical topic for a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea of a talk or essay, its subject.

clue.text: Vessel filled with chicken, cooker on the other hand…

indicators.note: the vessel is filled with the other pieces, which go inside it

parts.note: a tin is a container, a vessel
a hen is a chicken
an Aga is a brand of heavy cast-iron range cooker, common in British country kitchens

explanation.surface: A pot is loaded with chicken while the stove is put to other use.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a large British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Then again is an idiom introducing a contrary point, just as on the other hand does.

clue.text: Hard — as if camping?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: with close concentration, as in staring hard
second meaning, a punning one: in a tent-like manner

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as IN TENT plus the adverb ending LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To look intently is to look with fixed concentration, the same as looking hard.

clue.text: Paper pristine, step on it

parts.note: something pristine is new, unused
step on it means hurry, sprint

explanation.surface: Fresh paper on the floor, and someone is told to tread on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step on it' looks like a literal instruction, but it is the idiom for hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap paper on which newspapers are printed.

clue.text: Dull stuff, say, points reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed read as re-viewed, seen backwards, so the letters run from the end

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
dots are points

explanation.surface: Boring material, for instance, with its points looked over again.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, uninspired material, whether stodgy food or tedious writing.

clue.text: Agree ten is not right — one's somewhat older

indicators.note: the letters are not in their right order, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone disputes that ten is the correct figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because a teenager is a little older than a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is aged thirteen to nineteen, rather older than a child but not yet adult.

clue.text: Clever little mammal evolved, finally

parts.note: a shrew is a tiny insect-eating mammal

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of evolved

explanation.surface: A small creature at last developed some intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute and sharp in judgement, so it is a synonym for clever.

clue.text: Salvage lace that's woven into hem

indicators.note: into places the woven lace inside the hem

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border, like a hem

indicators.note: woven lace has its threads interlaced, a sign its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A seamstress rescues some lace by stitching it into a hem.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or rescue it from waste, the sense of salvage.

clue.text: In a kerfuffle, search bags always

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the search word bags, holds, the always word

parts.note: to fish is to search for, as in fishing for compliments
ever means always

explanation.surface: In a flap, someone rummages through handbags endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like a noun, handbags being searched, but it is the verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means frantically excited or agitated, which describes being in a flustered state.

clue.text: Mark I make bringing in voting system

indicators.note: the make word brings in, holds within it, the voting system

parts.note: to mint is to make, as coins are
PR is the abbreviation for proportional representation

explanation.surface: A voter vows to make their mark by introducing electoral reform.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is an impression left by pressure, a mark.

clue.text: Time I had with daughter during month

indicators.note: during places these pieces inside the month

parts.note: May is a month
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the period they spent with their daughter one month.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is noon, a specific hour of the clock.

clue.text: Genesis, where nice point made

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned, formed into something new from these letters

explanation.surface: A speaker locates the origin of a well-made argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Inception is the beginning or origin of something, the same as its genesis.

clue.text: Brownish pigment, peas in the soup injected with one

indicators.note: one is injected, put inside, the jumbled peas
in the soup means in trouble, so the letters of peas are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pea soup has gone a brown colour after a dose of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is an idiom for in a mess, here signalling that PEAS becomes SEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment originally made from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Stand over six feet perhaps, small earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts small in front of the other piece

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
someone over six feet is tall

explanation.surface: A tall person stands, with a short one put ahead of him.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a stand at a market, a booth where goods are sold.

clue.text: Cloth kept here, as knitting is initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Fabric is stored here, just as knitting is to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a sturdy dull-brown fabric used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Stubborn type admits got wrong!

indicators.note: wrong tells us the letters are in the wrong order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An obstinate person finally owns up to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a stubborn type would hardly ever admit a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogmatist asserts opinions as unquestionable truths and will not budge, a stubborn person.

clue.text: Dirty dog put in solitary, gutted

indicators.note: the dog is put in, placed inside, the remains of solitary
gutted removes the insides, leaving only the first and last letters of solitary

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A filthy dog is shut away alone, and its owner is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as upset, but it empties solitary to SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Smutty means indecent or obscene, so dirty in the sense of a dirty joke.

clue.text: Connected right up

parts.note: up means in high spirits, elated

explanation.surface: Linked all the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means linked by some relationship, as relatives or associated ideas are.
